title: Telerobotic Stroke Intervention
summary: An inexpensive telerobotic system that would let a surgeon treat stroke patients remotely — a partnership between the University of Minnesota, the Minnesota Robotics Institute, and Medtronic.
body: Mechanical thrombectomy works, but only if the patient reaches a surgeon in time. For people far from a comprehensive stroke centre, that is often the part that fails. The question that started this project came from a neurosurgeon: could an inexpensive robot let him treat those patients without them being transported first?

The lab is building that robot with the Minnesota Robotics Institute and Medtronic. The system lets a surgeon insert and rotate a guidewire remotely, with artificial intelligence — imitation learning and reinforcement learning — gradually taking over the routine steps of the procedure so the clinician can concentrate on the decisions that matter.

A first working prototype was demonstrated in November 2025, with Dr. Andrew Grande driving guidewires robotically from a phone while Medtronic's leadership watched. The partnership spans neurosurgery, mechanical engineering, and computer science, and involves more than fifteen graduate and undergraduate students across those departments.
